sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Tardigrade: microscopic invertebrates, most under 0.5 mm (1/50 inch); four pairs of stubby clawed legs; live in films of water on moss and lichen, and in fresh water and the sea; first described by J. A. E. Goeze in 1773, who called them little water bears; feed by piercing plant cells with stylets and sucking the contents; survive drying by entering a tun state (cryptobiosis) with almost no metabolism, then revive in water; more than 1,000 species; https://www.britannica.com/animal/tardigrade

Jönsson et al. 2008, Current Biology, Tardigrades survive exposure to space in low Earth orbit (FOTON-M3, 2007): dried tardigrades survived open space vacuum, and some survived space vacuum plus solar UV radiation; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2008.06.048

Tsujimoto, Imura & Kanda 2016, Cryobiology, Recovery and reproduction of an Antarctic tardigrade retrieved from a moss sample frozen for over 30 years: tardigrades from moss collected in 1983 and stored frozen at -20 C were thawed in 2014; two revived and one reproduced; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cryobiol.2015.12.003

Natural History Museum (London), Tardigrades: active tardigrades are not especially tough, their resilience comes from the dried tun state; you can find them by soaking moss in water and looking with a microscope; https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/news/2019/september/tardigrades-are-not-invincible.html

title: The Moss on Your Roof Hides an Animal That Survived Outer Space 🐻
tiktok_caption: the moss on my roof is full of tiny animals that survived outer space 🐻🚀 one came back to life after 30 years frozen. Would you look at your moss under a microscope? 🔬 yes / 🙅 no

beats.say: The moss on your roof is full of tiny animals that survived space.
The tardigrade. People call it the water bear.
Most are about half a millimeter long.
Eight chubby legs, each with tiny claws.
It lives in the wet film on moss.
When the moss dries out, it curls into a ball.
Its body almost stops working, and waits.
Add water, and it wakes up.
Basically, it can pause its own life.
